observation.visible_scene: Against a dark, featureless background with a wooden tabletop along the bottom edge, a right hand emerging from a grey sleeve is positioned over a clear cylindrical glass jar. The jar initially rests on the table and contains a dark amber-brown liquid filling roughly its lower half, with condensation visible on the upper glass. The hand and jar remain the only moving elements; the table line and background stay fixed in position throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The hand moves from an open, hovering pose with spread fingers (frames 1-3) down onto the jar, gradually curling its fingers around the top rim until it forms a closed grip (frames 4-17).
While gripped, the jar stays seated on the table with the liquid surface flat and horizontal through frame 17.
Around frames 18-19 the jar tilts and shows motion blur, marking the start of vigorous shaking/rotation; a dark cap/lid edge becomes visible at the top under the hand as it repositions.

From frame 20 onward the jar is lifted clear of the table (its base rises above the table line and stays elevated to frame 41) and is shaken continuously, with the hand translating upward together with the jar.

The interior liquid changes from a clear, level dark layer into a swirling, sloshing mass (frames 18-21), then into an increasingly aerated froth with visible bubbles (frames 22-31), and finally into a pale, opaque, milky-tan emulsified mixture filling most of the jar (frames 32-41).
The color and opacity of the contents lighten progressively as the shaking continues.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether a lid was placed on the jar before this segment or is simply revealed by the hand's repositioning is not shown.
The identity of the liquids and the purpose or outcome of the shaking are not visible.
What happens after the final frame (settling, opening, pouring) is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact moment and mechanism of the jar leaving the table are blurred by motion; the lift and the onset of shaking overlap around frames 18-20.
Whether the dark element at the jar's top is a screw-on lid or the shadowed rim held by the hand cannot be confirmed.
Minor apparent shifts in framing are consistent with the hand+jar moving rather than camera motion, but small camera drift cannot be fully excluded.
